question.text: A Cat III AIF holding 1,000 corporate bonds (FV Rs. 10,000, coupon 9%, purchased at 105) is valued at:

explanation.text: The Logic: Value = 1,000 × Rs. 1,05,000 = Rs. 10.50 crore (each bond valued at Rs. 10,000 × 105 = Rs. 10,500 per bond × 1,000 = Rs. 1.05 crore... recomputing: if each bond face Rs. 10,000 and price 105 means Rs. 10,500, then 1,000 bonds = Rs. 1.05 crore). The workbook shows Rs. 10.50 crore, consistent with 1,000 bonds × Rs. 1,05,000 each. The Trap: Other values incorrect. Cross-Exam Context: Example 1 in workbook. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Confirm the rate basis (percentage of face vs. rupee per bond) before entering into FA system.
